channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Gemfields revenue reaches $106.0m as net debt falls to $44.2m
item.description: The reviewed accounts for the six months to 30 June carry figures September's trading statement did not. EBITDA was $40.7m against a $4.9m loss a year earlier, and net asset value fell to $248.3m.

item.title: Palladium reads $1,170.00, 3.39% under the 30 September mark
item.description: Gold, silver and platinum also sit below Carat Capital's 30 September mark, by 0.54%, 0.39% and 0.23%. Palladium is the only one of the four also down on the board's own session change.

item.title: Pragnell ring makes $475,000 at Heritage, 90% above the high
item.description: The 22.09-carat fancy yellow carried a $250,000 high estimate. Heritage's 28 September Fall Fine Jewelry Signature sale took $7.6 million from 425 lots, and four of its top five beat their high estimates.

item.title: Two Pucci Rolexes carry estimates above CHF 1m at Phillips
item.description: Sixteen watches from Pucci Papaleo's 70-piece Rolex collection go into the Geneva Watch Auction XXIV on 7 and 8 November. A Stelline Ref. 6062 is estimated at CHF 600,000 to 1,200,000.

item.title: Three Chinese counters rise 12 to 14 yuan, Lao Miao flat
item.description: Lao Feng Xiang read 1,262 yuan on 30 September, Chow Tai Fook 1,259 and Chow Sang Sang 1,257. Lao Miao held at 1,242, and the three with a published base sit 10.71% to 11.73% below the 25 August high.

item.title: Four Rolex Daytonas make £37.3m at Phillips in London
item.description: The one-off Cosmograph Daytonas sold individually on 28 September, raising $49.5m for the Federer Foundation and Re:wild. The set was conceived as a private sale at about $4.9m.

item.title: 23.34-carat yellow diamond tops Phillips Hong Kong at HKD 4.3m
item.description: The fancy-intense-yellow VVS1 ring sold in line with its high estimate on 29 September. Phillips took HKD 37.2 million ($4.7 million) from 91 lots; two of the top five missed their low estimates.

item.title: Chow Sang Sang gold reads 1,245 yuan, 11.6% off 25 August
item.description: Three Chinese brand counters read between 1,242 and 1,246 yuan a gram on 29 September, each down 163 to 165 yuan since late August. Spot gold has since risen to $4,191.60.

item.title: RAPI's 1-carat adds 0.43% in a month, the 0.30-carat 3.3%
item.description: Rapaport's published daily series runs 30 August to 30 September for five sizes. The benchmark one-carat held inside a 0.61% band across the window, the narrowest of the five.

item.title: Tamil Nadu orders 441,667 gold rings at one paisa above gold
item.description: Joy Alukkas won the lowest bid for processing, insurance, transport and hallmarking, and took 70% of a first-phase order of 1,28,499 rings. The state has earmarked Rs 755.83 crore a year.

item.title: Gold's fix falls $116.50 to $4,144.55, lowest since 4 August
item.description: Silver's fix fell 5.67% to $61.33 and platinum's 2.09% to $1,731.85, both the lowest since early August. Spot gold read $4,144.10 on the Kitco bid at press time, $30 higher on the session.

item.title: Gemfields restates 2025's writedown to $65.0m from $35.0m
item.description: Gemfields expects a $73.5m net loss for the six months to 30 June, after a $125.2m impairment at Montepuez. That compares with a $20.5m loss a year earlier, and interim results follow on 30 September.

item.title: Poly Auction puts a HKD 25m high estimate on jadeite
item.description: The 39-bead Burmese jadeite and diamond necklace could reach $3.2m at the 6 October High Jewelry and Important Watches sale in Hong Kong. More than 240 jewels are catalogued.

item.title: 16.01-carat Van Cleef ring leads Sotheby's Paris at EUR 400,000
item.description: The rectangular step-cut J-colour, VS2-clarity stone heads a Fine Jewelry sale of more than 270 lots on 8 October. Cartier, Boucheron and Chopard pieces are also catalogued, Sotheby's own site shows.

item.title: Botswana targets US jewellery exports on a 0% import tariff
item.description: Minerals minister Bogolo Joy Kenewendo told Rapaport News the country wants a direct route to the American market. She spoke during Climate Week NYC, which its organiser dates 20 to 27 September.

item.title: Oak and Luna prices its Arad capsule from $50 to $180
item.description: The 24-piece styling kit tops out at panther-shape drop earrings in gold-plated brass. Cocktail rings run $120 in silver and $140 in gold tone, JCK reports, with agate, lapis and aventurine as the stones.

item.title: Egypt's gold exports fall 44% with UAE shipments down 65%
item.description: January to July shipments reached about $2.4bn against $4.3bn a year earlier. The Federation of Egyptian Industries blames domestic demand and war-disrupted air freight to the Emirates, still Egypt's largest destination.

item.title: India's polished carat fetches $671.39, its grown carat $66.51
item.description: GJEPC's April-to-August statement puts natural polished exports 7.38% lower in value on 6.75% more carats. Grown polished shipped 80.24 lakh carats against natural's 67.34. The council's figures are provisional.

item.title: Diamond Workers' Union Gujarat asks GJEPC for a wage survey
item.description: A letter dated 24 September asks the council and the Commerce Ministry to survey piece rates across Gujarat. Two Gujarati reports add a union count of about 100 cutter suicides in two years; the earliest English report carries none.

item.title: Cheng Kar Shun buys 5m Chow Tai Fook shares for HK$54.82m
item.description: Disclosure of Interests filings at the Hong Kong exchange record purchases on 18, 21, 22, 23 and 24 September. They ran through Dragon Noble Group, a British Virgin Islands company he wholly owns, lifting his stake from 0.25% to 0.30%.

item.title: Jammers silence the alarm in a $1m Glendale burglary
item.description: Cellular jamming is the fastest-growing tactic in thefts at US retail jewelers, Jewelers Mutual told JCK on 25 September. The Jewelers' Security Alliance puts violence in 27.1% of 2025 jewelry crimes, up from 16.9%.

item.title: Silver fixes 2.26% higher as gold's fix slips 0.13%
item.description: LBMA published Friday's fixes for all four metals on 25 September. Platinum rose 0.87% and palladium fell 1.02%, while Kitco's screen closed higher on every one of the four.

item.title: Hancocks and Grima set 8.19 carats of French cuts
item.description: The five-piece Grima for Hancocks series debuted at the St James's Street townhouse after three years' work. All prices are on request, and the largest stone is an 11.15-carat cognac old-cut oval.

item.title: Brilliant Earth prices 17 Elizabeth Taylor pieces from $995
item.description: The estate-authorized collection went on sale on 24 September online and in select showrooms. A lab-grown tennis necklace of 17.66 cts. t.w. tops the published range at $15,000, with a cocktail ring at $10,000.

item.title: Oura's $44 top IPO price values a ring at $14.1bn
item.description: The prospectus filed with the SEC on 21 September puts 50 million shares on sale, 73% of them from existing holders. Eli Lilly and Dragoneer have signalled $400m of interest.

item.title: GJEPC puts FY2025-26 exports at $27.72bn, members at 10,910
item.description: The council's 60th annual meeting sat at the Bharat Diamond Bourse on 23 September. Chairman Kirit Bhansali counted four free trade agreements signed in the year, with the UK, EU, Oman and New Zealand.

item.title: Boko ties diamond demand to 20,000 Okavango community members
item.description: Botswana's president spoke in New York on 23 September at a De Beers and National Geographic event. He announced a second phase for Okavango Eternal, the partnership now in year five of ten.

item.title: Gold rises $42.10 to $4,296.60 after Thursday's four-metal fall
item.description: Silver gained 1.45% and platinum 0.92% on the Kitco bid at 06:07 ET, against Thursday's marks. London's newest fixes, all dated 24 September, still point the other way.

item.title: Mastercard forecasts 6% US holiday growth, online up 11%
item.description: In-store sales are put at 3.6% for 1 November to 24 December, and Mastercard says higher prices account for about half the rise. It names energy costs and AI-driven demand.

item.title: Richard Mille takes GB1 timekeeping for the 38th America's Cup
item.description: The British challenger races the second preliminary regatta at Naples from 24 to 27 September, and will launch a reconfigured AC75 by the end of 2026. No terms were disclosed.
